# Worker Agents Skills

This repository bundles the baseline skills installed by [Worker
Agents](https://github.com/agents-dev/workerAgents).

The bundled skills are available under [`skills/`](skills/):

- `mcp-duckgo` — imported from `aahl/skills@mcp-duckgo`.
- `image-search` — imported from `z0gsh1u/oh-my-writing-skill@image-search`.
- `gauntlet-loop` — imported from `robonuggets/gauntlet-loop@gauntlet-loop`.
- `load-sketchfab-threejs` — local asset inspection, normalization, and Three.js/PlayCanvas A/B viewer skill.
- `opencode-zen-completions` — use the OpenCode Zen chat completions API for implementation work.

The original upstream licenses are preserved in
[`third-party-licenses/`](third-party-licenses/).
---
opencode.yml
name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
      issue_number: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
      OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON }}
      AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ secrets.AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY }}
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}

## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)

initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the

the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build?

## Objective
- Build a polished GTA V–inspired open-world browser game ("LOS SANTOS STREETS") in Three.js for the PlayGround repo, playable on desktop and mobile.
- User's only request text: "Gta 5" (GitHub issue title/body), labeled `mobile`; deliver a complete, working game and verify it visually.

## Requirements
- GTA V-style open world: city, cars, driving, shooting, police/wanted system, missions, money, HUD.
- Mobile support: responsive layouts, touch joystick, touch camera drag, on-screen action buttons, safe-area insets, landscape guidance.
- Must run as a static site (no framework) and be visually verified in a real browser.
- Long-lived servers must run in tmux; use `playwright-cli` from the preinstalled setup for captures; reject blank/loading screens.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JS site with vendored Three.js r170 and selected addons (no build step).
- Modular JS: world, player, vehicles, peds, police, missions, HUD, effects, audio, main.
- Custom arcade physics, procedural city, instanced meshes for buildings/windows/props, postprocessing (bloom + planned color grade), synthesized WebAudio.
- Golden-hour Los Santos art direction; mobile HUD/controls repositioned via `body.touch`.
- Unit/actor hit proxies (invisible meshes) used for raycast shooting.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vendored Three.js r170 and addons under `vendor/`; fixed addon folder layout to `vendor/addons/postprocessing/` and `vendor/addons/shaders/`.
- Built full game skeleton: procedural city (roads, sidewalks, buildings, windows, palms, lamps, park, plaza tower, mountains placeholder, hillside sign), player character+weapons, car models/physics/traffic/parked cars, civilians/gang/cop actors, police wanted system, 4 missions (Repo Man, Street Sweep, Vinewood Run, Heat), HUD/radar, effects, audio, input (keyboard/mouse/touch), start/pause/wasted screens.
- Unit-like pages load with 0 console errors; game starts, renders city, player, HUD, mission marker, traffic.
- Added vendored fonts: `fonts/anton.woff2`, `fonts/barlow-600.woff2`, `fonts/barlow-700.woff2`; CSS `@font-face` added and display font stacks changed to Anton.
- Added `#ui.hidden` initially and removed on game start to hide HUD behind menu.
- Reworked sky/lighting: low sun aligned with sprite, warmer sky/fog, stronger directional light; added asphalt/sidewalk/window textures helpers (`asphaltTexture`, `tileTexture`, `windowTexture`).
- Started upgrading buildings: new palette, window texture, storefront instanced mesh, cornice/base trims (partially wired; see Active).

### Active
- Finishing `js/world.js` building upgrade: storefront/cornice/base instance placement inside `addBuilding`, then add instances to scene and set counts.
- Then apply mountain/hill replacement, palm crown material fix, traffic-light props, and menu camera/high-vantage + color-grade shader.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Finish `addBuilding` in `js/world.js`: place cornice, base band, and 4 storefront planes per building; add `stores`, `cornices`, `bases` to `this.root`; set `.count`, instanceColor needsUpdate.
2. Replace pyramid-like `buildMountains()` cones with overlapping flattened hemisphere/icosahedron hills (muted blue-green, farther out); keep/reposition "LOS SANTOS" sign.
3. Lighten palm crowns (`0x4f7d38`+emissive) and refine frond shape; optionally add intersection traffic lights.
4. Change menu/intro camera to high wide sunset skyline orbit; add subtle grade ShaderPass before `OutputPass` (saturation/contrast/cool shadows/warm highlights/vignette).
5. Improve character model proportions (rounded torso, shoulder spheres, better limbs) in `js/character.js`.
6. Re-test with `playwright-cli` (server already running in tmux `untitled` on port 3002): menu screenshot, click play, screenshot gameplay; test walk to M, start/complete mission, enter/drive car, shoot, wanted stars, pause, mobile emulation.
7. Use a harsh visual critic subagent on screenshots and iterate.
8. Check/repair gameplay bugs (car steering sign, camera, mission flow) and mobile layout; commit changes (none committed yet).

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`: city, lighting, textures, collision, pickups; actively being edited.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: bootstrap, renderer/composer, camera, input (pointer-lock fallback), loop, game wiring.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/player.js`: third-person controller, weapons/shooting, health/death.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/vehicles.js`: car models, player driving, traffic AI, explosions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/peds.js`: civilians, gang, cops, animation/combat.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/police.js`: wanted stars, cop spawn/chase/evade.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/missions.js`: mission definitions/state/markers.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/character.js`: humanoid builder, pistol/SMG models.

- Known code quirks: pointer-lock may be blocked in iframe; fallback drag-look/click-shoot implemented via `game.lockFailed`.
- Player position is synced to car while driving (`player.update` inCar branch) for missions/radar/shadow focus.
- Git changes are uncommitted; branch `main`, issue #5.

333:     const buildingGeo = new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1)

390:     const addWindow = (x, y, z, rotY, c) => {
391:       if (wi >= 14000) return

393:       tmpM.compose(tmpV.set(x, y, z), tmpQ, tmpS.set(1, 1, 1))

399:     const addBuilding = (cx, cz, w, d, h, tone) => {

407:       this.colliders.push({
408:         min: new THREE.Vector3(cx - w / 2, 0, cz - d / 2),
409:         max: new THREE.Vector3(cx + w / 2, h, cz + d / 2)
410:       })
411: 
412:       const faces = [
413:         { n: [0, 0, 1], rot: 0, width: w, off: d / 2 + 0.015, x: cx },
414:         { n: [0, 0, -1], rot: Math.PI, width: w, off: d / 2 + 0.015, x: cx },
415:         { n: [1, 0, 0], rot: Math.PI / 2, width: d, off: w / 2 + 0.015, x: cz },
416:         { n: [-1, 0, 0], rot: -Math.PI / 2, width: d, off: w / 2 + 0.015, x: cz }
417:       ]
418:       for (const f of faces) {
419:         const cols = Math.max(1, Math.floor(f.width / 3.1))
420:         const rows = Math.max(1, Math.floor((h - 5) / 3.6))
421:         for (let r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
422:           for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
423:             if (wi >= 14000) break
424:             const along = (c - (cols - 1) / 2) * (f.width / cols)
425:             const y = 4.7 + r * 3.6
426:             if (f.n[2] !== 0) {
427:               addWindow(cx + along, y, cz + f.off * f.n[2], f.rot, pick(windowColors))

429:               addWindow(cx + f.off * f.n[0], y, cz + along, f.rot, pick(windowColors))
430:             }
431:           }
432:         }
433:         // storefront strip
434:         if (Math.random() < 0.55 && ai < 160) {
435:           const shopColor = pick([0x1fb6a6, 0xd94f3d, 0xe8a33d, 0x2f7fbf, 0xb34fbf, 0x3fa35b, 0xefe6d2])
436:           const sw = Math.min(f.width * 0.7, 9)
437:           if (f.n[2] !== 0) {
438:             tmpM.makeScale(sw, 1, 0.6)
439:             tmpM.setPosition(cx, 3.1, cz + (d / 2 + 0.32) * f.n[2])
440:           } else {
441:             tmpM.makeScale(0.6, 1, sw)
442:             tmpM.setPosition(cx + (w / 2 + 0.32) * f.n[0], 3.1, cz)
443:           }
444:           awnings.setMatrixAt(ai, tmpM)
445:           awnings.setColorAt(ai, color.setHex(shopColor))
446:           ai++
447:         }
448:       }
449: 
450:       // Rooftop clutter
451:       const n = Math.floor(rand(0, 3))
452:       for (let k = 0; k < n && aci < 180; k++) {
453:         const sw = rand(1.5, 3.4), sh = rand(0.8, 2.2), sd = rand(1.5, 3.4)
454:         tmpM.makeScale(sw, sh, sd)
455:         tmpM.setPosition(cx + rand(-w / 3, w / 3), h + 0.26 + sh / 2, cz + rand(-d / 3, d / 3))
456:         acs.setMatrixAt(aci++, tmpM)
457:       }
458:     }
459: 
460:     for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
461:       for (let j = 0; j < 5; j++) {
462:         const x0 = GRID[i], x1 = GRID[i + 1], z0 = GRID[j], z1 = GRID[j + 1]
463:         const bx0 = x0 + ROAD_W / 2 + WALK, bx1 = x1 - ROAD_W / 2 - WALK
464:         const bz0 = z0 + ROAD_W / 2 + WALK, bz1 = z1 - ROAD_W / 2 - WALK

467:         if (i === 2 && j === 2) { this.buildPlaza(bx0, bz0, bx1, bz1); continue }
468: 
469:         const lots = 2

471:         const lotW = (bx1 - bx0 - gap) / lots
472:         for (let l = 0; l < lots; l++) {
473:           const lx0 = bx0 + l * (lotW + gap)
474:           const lx1 = lx0 + lotW
475:           const w = Math.min(lotW - rand(1, 3.5), 17)
476:           const d = Math.min(bz1 - bz0 - rand(1, 5), 34)
477:           const cx = (lx0 + lx1) / 2 + rand(-1, 1)
478:           const cz = (bz0 + bz1) / 2 + rand(-1.5, 1.5)
479:           const dist = Math.hypot(cx, cz) / 220
480:           let h = 9 + Math.pow(1 - Math.min(dist, 1), 2) * rand(24, 70) + rand(0, 10)
481:           if (Math.random() < 0.12) h = rand(7, 12)
482:           addBuilding(cx, cz, w, d, h, pick(bodyColors))
483:         }
484:       }
485:     }
486: 
487:     bodies.count = bi
488:     bodies.instanceColor.needsUpdate = true
489:     windows.count = wi
490:     windows.instanceColor.needsUpdate = true
491:     awnings.count = ai
492:     awnings.instanceColor.needsUpdate = true
493:     acs.count = aci
494:     this.root.add(bodies, windows, awnings, acs)
495:     this.windowMesh = windows
496:   }

582:   buildPalms() {

584:     // slight bend for palm trunks
585:     const pos = trunkGeo.attributes.position
586:     for (let i = 0; i < pos.count; i++) {
587:       const y = pos.getY(i)
588:       const t = (y + 0.5)

592:     const trunkMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x6d5234, roughness: 1 })

595:     // Build a merged frond crown

597:     const n = 9

609:     const crownMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x39652f, roughness: 0.95, side: THREE.DoubleSide, flatShading: true })

715:     const rocks = new THREE.InstancedMesh(rockGeo, rockMat, 90)

## Objective
- Build a polished GTA V–inspired open-world browser game ("LOS SANTOS STREETS") in Three.js for the PlayGround repo, playable on desktop and mobile.
- User's only request text: "Gta 5" (GitHub issue title/body), labeled `mobile`; deliver a complete, working game and verify it visually.

## Requirements
- GTA V-style open world: city, cars, driving, shooting, police/wanted system, missions, money, HUD.
- Mobile support: responsive layouts, touch joystick, touch camera drag, on-screen action buttons, safe-area insets, landscape guidance.
- Must run as a static site (no framework) and be visually verified in a real browser.
- Long-lived servers must run in tmux; use `playwright-cli` from the preinstalled setup for captures; reject blank/loading screens.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JS site with vendored Three.js r170 and selected addons (no build step).
- Modular JS: world, player, vehicles, peds, police, missions, HUD, effects, audio, main.
- Custom arcade physics, procedural city, instanced meshes, postprocessing (bloom + custom color-grade shader).
- Golden-hour Los Santos art direction; mobile HUD/controls repositioned via `body.touch`.
- Use direct API/teleport shortcuts during testing because headless rendering is ~5.5 FPS and simulated time runs slowly.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full playable game skeleton: procedural city, player + weapons, cars/driving/traffic/parked cars, civilians/gang/cops, police wanted system, four missions, HUD/radar, effects, synthesized audio, pause/wasted screens.
- Desktop menu, gameplay, driving, mission start/completion verified visually with 0 console errors on load.
- Mission flow verified end-to-end via API: REPO MAN completes, reward +$650, money reaches $1,150, objective marker now hides correctly.
- Fixed critical driving bug: `addVehicle` now merges `CAR_TYPES` stats (`accel`, `brake`, `maxSpeed`, `grip`, `steerRate`); previously missing stats produced NaN car physics and audio errors.
- Added `Number.isFinite` guard around engine audio speed to prevent `setTargetAtTime` NaN errors.
- Fixed mission completion bug where the objective marker reappeared after `completeMission`; added `if (!this.active || !this.mission) return` guard.
- Reworked mission marker beacon into a slim shader-based light column with vertical alpha fade.
- Added building upgrades: storefront planes, awnings, cornices, base bands, rooftop AC units, improved window/store textures.
- Replaced pyramid mountains with overlapping procedural smooth hill domes; repositioned "LOS SANTOS" hillside sign.
- Fixed palm crowns (white base material × instance colors) and refined fronds.
- Added traffic-light props at all intersections.
- Improved player model proportions with rounded torso/chest, shoulder caps, segmented arms/legs, larger head, facial details.
- Added color-grade ShaderPass (saturation/contrast/split-tone/vignette) and tuned lighting/fog/exposure to a warmer, higher-contrast sunset.
- Menu camera changed to high wide skyline orbit.
- Added parked cars near spawn and scripted pedestrians on nearby sidewalks.
- Mobile portrait and landscape menus verified; fixed landscape menu clipping with `@media (max-height: 500px)`.
- Mobile landscape gameplay verified: joystick movement works, hold-FIRE shoots, HUD/buttons/safe-area layout visible.
- Mission splash now has a dark radial backdrop; "MISSION STARTED" toast removed.
- Added `HUD.clearToasts()` and call it on mission start.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
/usr/bin/time -p node "${RUNTIME_DIR:?}/scripts/default-capture.mjs"
---
## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.
